# CANDIDATE: PROFIT_LOCK_TRAIL_10

**Filed:** 2026-07-22  
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)  
**Type:** parameter_change  
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

Reducing the profit-lock trail percentage from 0.15 to 0.10 in the BEARISH_REJECTION_RIDE_THE_RIBBON setup will allow the runner to capture more of the trend on winning days while still providing adequate protection on losing days, thereby increasing edge_capture on J anchor days without significantly increasing losers.

## Mechanism

Change the profit-lock trail parameter in the BEARISH_REJECTION_RIDE_THE_RIBBON setup from 0.15 to 0.10. The profit-lock arms at +5% favor (as currently) and trails the high-water mark by the new trail percentage (0.10 × current premium). All other rules (chart stop, TP1 at +50%, time stop, etc.) remain unchanged. This change affects both Safe and Bold accounts identically since profit-lock parameters are shared.

## OP-20 disclosures

1. **Account-size assumption:** qty=28 requires $25K+; $1K paper ~= 14% headline (based on BEARISH_REJECTION_RIDE_THE_RIBBON setup's 3-contract minimum and $500 max risk per trade at $1K account)
2. **Sample bias:** Proposed change based on trend-capture hypothesis; no historical test yet → high overfit risk if tuned to J days; requires Stage-1 backtest to quantify bias
3. **Out-of-sample:** NEEDS-OOS (no OOS test performed)
4. **Real-fills:** NEEDS-REAL-FILLS (no real OPRA fill validation)
5. **Failure modes:** 
   - Worst day: Tighter trail may cause premature exits on noise, converting winners to losers (e.g., 4/29 if intra-bar fluctuation triggers stop)
   - Max drawdown: Could increase if losing days see larger losses due to earlier exits
   - Blow-up: Sequence of stopped-out winners in choppy market could create consecutive losses
6. **Concentration:** TBD after Stage-1 backtest (will compute top5_pct of P&L)

## Pre-merge gate
